title: Restriction of scalars commutes with $f_*$
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings with coefficient
changes $a_X$ ([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]), and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of schemes.
With $f_*$ the pushforward of module objects ([sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]), there
is a natural isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y}\circ f_*\;\cong\;f_*\circ\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}\colon
\Mod_{\Lambda'_X}\longrightarrow\Mod_{\Lambda_Y},
$$

under which both sides are $\mathrm{mapMod}(f_*)$ followed by the restriction of scalars along
$\eta'_f\circ a_Y=f_*a_X\circ\eta_f\colon\Lambda_Y\to f_*\Lambda'_X$.

proof.text: Write $F=f^{\Ab}_*\colon\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)\to\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ for pushforward of abelian sheaves. The coefficient maps have types $\eta_f\colon\Lambda_Y\to F\Lambda_X$ and $\eta'_f\colon\Lambda'_Y\to F\Lambda'_X$, as in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. By [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], the functor $F$ acts on abelian sheaves, is lax monoidal, and the module pushforward is defined as $\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$; applying that clause to $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda'$ gives $f_*^\Lambda=\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ and $f_*^{\Lambda'}=\operatorname{Res}_{\eta'_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$. Thus the two functors to be compared have the form required by the restriction/transport square, with source $\Mod_{\Lambda'_X}$ and target $\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}$. Here $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ is restriction from modules over the codomain of $\varphi$ to modules over its domain, with action $\gamma_N\circ(\varphi\otimes N)$ and unchanged underlying objects and arrows, as in clause 1 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars].

source.place: proof, the pushforward formula and specialization of the commutative-square construction

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-coefficient-pushforward-square], applied to the condensed abelian-group morphism underlying the ring morphism $a$, the coefficient maps satisfy $F(a_X)\circ\eta_f=\eta'_f\circ a_Y\colon\Lambda_Y\to F\Lambda'_X$. By [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], $\eta_f$ and $\eta'_f$ are ring-object morphisms, and [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] says that $a_X$ and $a_Y$ are ring-object morphisms. Thus the maps $R_X=\Lambda_X$, $S_X=\Lambda'_X$, $R_Y=\Lambda_Y$, $S_Y=\Lambda'_Y$, $\varphi_X=a_X$, $\varphi_Y=a_Y$, $\eta_R=\eta_f$, and $\eta_S=\eta'_f$ form the commutative square of monoid-object morphisms used in the next step. Here the square lemma's $f_*$ on coefficient objects and arrows is precisely the abelian-sheaf functor $F$, not either of the two module pushforwards; its ring-coefficient clause identifies its $\eta$ maps with those in step 1.

source.place: proof, the pushforward formula and specialization of the commutative-square construction

proof.text: Define the comparison to be the isomorphism of [def-sfb-comap-mapmod-square] for the square in step 2 and the lax monoidal functor in step 1. Substitution in its source and target gives $\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y}\circ f_*^{\Lambda'}\cong f_*^\Lambda\circ\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}$. Its statement also identifies both functors with transport by $\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ followed by restriction along the common composite $\eta'_f\circ a_Y=F(a_X)\circ\eta_f\colon\Lambda_Y\to F\Lambda'_X$, exactly the specified normalization. Naturality and invertibility are supplied by that natural isomorphism.
